segments.text: In this town, your body count floats above your head. Mine is zero. My grandma's is forty-seven.
Nobody really knows what it counts. The kids at school make jokes about it. The grown-ups never do. They just say: pray yours stays at zero.
Grandma Rose is the sweetest person in town. She knits sweaters for everyone, and she bakes a cherry pie for every new neighbor.
Funny thing is, the new neighbors never stay long. They always move away in the middle of the night. No goodbye.
And Grandma's garden is always freshly dug. Even in winter.
Last week, the Parkers moved in next door. Their son Max was my age. We became best friends in one afternoon.
That evening, Grandma brought them a cherry pie.
The next morning, their house was empty. Moved away, Grandma said. And above her head, the number said forty-eight.
That's when I finally understood what it counts.
Tonight, Grandma made another cherry pie. She put a big slice in front of me and smiled.
I looked at her number. Forty-eight. Then it started to flicker.
